correctness.rationale: In the finite-cofinite Boolean algebra on \(\omega\), \(\operatorname{At}(\mathfrak A)\) is the singleton family and \(\operatorname{Mid}(\mathfrak A)\) is countably infinite and bijective with it. Hence the set \(\operatorname{Bij}\) of all bijections \(\operatorname{Mid}(\mathfrak A)\to\operatorname{At}(\mathfrak A)\) has cardinality \(2^{\aleph_0}\): pair-swaps encode every subset of \(\omega\), while each bijection is a subset of \(\omega\times\omega\). Krawczyk proves that distinct indices give distinct minimal varieties and that no neighborhood frame validates the corresponding logic. Fritz’s theorem, reproduced in the same article, gives exactly \(2^{\aleph_0}\) C-Post complete congruential modal logics in total. Therefore the unsound subclass has matching lower and upper bounds.

value.rationale: Fritz explicitly asked how many neighborhood-incomplete/unsound C-Post complete logics there are. The exact cardinality is therefore a natural invariant attached to a stated open problem, not an arbitrary slice. Showing that Krawczyk’s family has the maximum possible size \(2^{\aleph_0}\) gives a CH-independent exact answer for the unsound branch and sharpens the source’s merely uncountable formulation.
